prompt: Construct the truth table, including every listed intermediate column: ~p; p -> q; ~p v q. Show your row order.

solution.text: Use row order p, q with T before F. Compute ~ first, then ^, then v, then ->, then <-> unless parentheses specify otherwise.

title: False antecedent

solution.text: Implication is equivalent to ~p v q.
This OR is false only if ~p=F and q=F.
Thus p=T,q=F is the unique false row.

subject: dm
title: Knights: implication with three inhabitants
prompt: A says "B is a knight." B says "If A is a knight, so is C." A,B,C are each knights or knaves. Determine their types.

solution.text: Let a,b,c denote that A,B,C respectively are knights. Then a=b and b=(a->c).
If a=F, then b=F, but a->c is T. This contradicts B being a knave.
Therefore a=T and b=T. B's implication with a=T forces c=T.
Hence A,B,C are all knights, uniquely.

subject: dm
title: Knight, knave and spy
prompt: Exactly one of A,B,C is a knight, one a knave, one a spy. A says "I am the knight"; B says "A is not the knave"; C says "B is not the knave". Find every consistent assignment.

solution.text: If A is the knight, B cannot be the knave because B's statement would be true. Then B is the spy and C is the knave, but C's statement is true, impossible.
If A is the knave, B says something false and so must be the spy; C is then the knight. All three statements fit their types. This gives (A=N,B=S,C=K).
If A is the spy, B's statement is true, so B must be the knight and C the knave. But C's statement is true, impossible.
Therefore the unique solution is A=knave, B=spy, C=knight.
